hooks.command: echo '🚀 DevOps session started at '$(date) && if [ -f main.tf ]; then echo '🏗️ Terraform project detected'; elif [ -f Dockerfile ]; then echo '🐳 Docker project detected'; elif [ -d k8s/ ] || [ -d manifests/ ]; then echo '☸️ Kubernetes project detected'; fi

hooks.prompt: Evaluate if this bash command is safe for production environments. BLOCK these dangerous commands: 'terraform destroy' without specific -target, 'terraform apply' with -auto-approve in production, 'kubectl delete namespace' in production, 'kubectl exec' on production pods without justification, 'rm -rf /' or 'rm -rf' on critical paths, 'docker system prune -af', 'git push --force' to main/master, any command that could cause irreversible data loss. Return 'approve' if safe or 'block' with reason.

hooks.command: FILE="$CLAUDE_TOOL_FILE_PATH"; if [[ "$FILE" == *.tf ]]; then terraform fmt "$FILE" 2>/dev/null && terraform validate 2>/dev/null && echo '✅ Terraform: formatted and validated'; elif [[ "$FILE" == *.yaml || "$FILE" == *.yml ]]; then if [[ "$FILE" == *github/workflows* ]]; then actionlint "$FILE" 2>/dev/null && echo '✅ GitHub Actions workflow valid'; else kubectl apply --dry-run=client -f "$FILE" 2>/dev/null && echo '✅ K8s manifest valid'; fi; elif [[ "$FILE" == *Dockerfile* ]]; then hadolint "$FILE" 2>/dev/null && echo '✅ Dockerfile linted'; fi

hooks.prompt: Before stopping, verify task completion: 1) If Terraform was modified: did terraform validate pass? 2) If K8s manifests were edited: are they valid? 3) No secrets, API keys, or credentials exposed in any file? 4) All requested tasks completed? Return 'approve' to stop or 'block' with reason to continue.
Verify subagent task completion. Did the subagent fully complete its assigned task? Are there any errors or incomplete outputs? Return 'approve' to stop or 'block' with reason.
